headings: HorizonStream: Long-Horizon Attention for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
B.4 Formal Connection to Test-Time Training

figures.caption: Figure 1: Geometric evidence influence patterns on KITTI and long-sequence scaling on VBR. Prior streaming methods impose hard cutoffs, refresh discontinuities, heavy-tailed states, or spiky KV caches, leading to pose degradation, jitter, or collapse. HorizonStream learns a bounded multi-scale kernel with an O⁡(1)O(1) recurrent geometric state and maintains stable ATE up to 10​K10\mathrm{K} frames.

Figure 2: Visualization of long-range streaming 3D reconstruction across diverse scenes. Our method maintains stable trajectories and coherent geometry over sequences ranging from hundreds to thousands of frames in outdoor, indoor, and game environments.

Figure 3: Overview of HorizonStream. Given an RGB stream, the model causally processes the most recent WW frames. Gated Window Attention handles local matching, Geometric Linear Attention propagates long-range geometry with an O⁡(1)O(1) recurrent geometric state, and Metric Readout Tokens recover stable scale and pose. An optional loop-closure module refines the trajectory.

Figure 4: Qualitative comparison on long-sequence 3D reconstruction. As sequence length grows, existing methods show pose degradation, drift, or collapse. Lingbot-map exhibits progressively stronger pose jitter over longer rollouts, while HorizonStream maintains stable pose estimation. For HorizonStream, dashed lines denote results without loop closure.

Figure 5: Qualitative comparison on 3D reconstruction. Left: trajectory. Right: 3D reconstruction. HorizonStream maintains stable geometry. Lingbot-map preserves trajectory direction but exhibits increasing jitter, causing point cloud overlap. For HorizonStream, dashed trajectory lines denote results without loop closure, and solid trajectory lines denote results with loop closure.

KV-cache contamination. Refresh/no-refresh variants of CUT3R, TTT3R, and LoGeR isolate periodic state reset. Without refresh, all three degrade sharply, indicating temporal-state contamination rather than limited model capacity. (a) (b) (c) Figure 6: (a) Learned retention spectra in Geometric Linear Attention. Effective lifetimes τ=−1/logγ¯\tau=-1/\log\bar{\gamma} vary across channels and layers. Layer 4 exhibits broad mid-range retention, while Layer 11 develops a pronounced long-retention tail, supporting channel-wise multi-timescale propagation. (b) Retention-band ablation. Replacing the learned channel-wise retention spectrum with fixed short-, medium-, or long-horizon bands increases trajectory error, showing that stable long-sequence propagation requires learned multi-timescale retention. (c) Long-sequence stability of Gated Window Attention. Head-wise gating and 3D RoPE are complementary: removing either causes error growth over time, while using both keeps the model stable.

Figure 7: GPU memory and runtime scaling. HorizonStream keeps peak GPU memory nearly constant and scales smoothly to 10​K10\mathrm{K} frames, while competing methods require increasing GPU memory or higher runtime on long sequences.

Figure 8: Training convergence under different attention mechanisms. In the legend, GGLA and GLGA denote Geometric Linear Attention (GLA) and Gated Window Attention (GWA), respectively; SWA denotes the sliding-window attention baseline. GLA with channel-wise gating converges faster and reaches a lower final loss.
Figure 9: Effect of loop closure on long sequences. Loop closure reduces ATE on sequences with revisited regions while maintaining performance elsewhere.

Figure 10: Failure cases on ultra-long sequences. Ground-truth trajectory (red), online prediction (blue), and loop-closure refined trajectory (green). Failures occur mainly in sequences with dense revisits or visually ambiguous regions.

Figure 11: Linear probing of frozen Geometric Linear Attention states. Ridge regressors trained on chunk-level state features predict four geometric error targets. Segment-scale log error is the most reliably predictable, suggesting that the recurrent state encodes measurable metric information. Other targets are less consistently captured by a linear probe. Figure 12: Probe weight attribution by retention band (segment scale target). Weights are nearly uniform across short / medium / long, showing that scale signal is distributed rather than band-specific.
